title: Swabians, Saxons, and Hessians have not stated this quarrel in one shared way
pass_a_gloss: From which it is plain how entangled the state of the controversy has been made by others, and how it has not always been set out in one way by the Lutherans. For the Swabians — Brentius, Schmidlinus, and so on, the first authors — wanted an effusion of the divine properties into the human, by force of the union, already in the womb; the Saxons a communion of the divine properties of omnipotence, omnipresence, and so on, in the assumed flesh, by force of the exaltation and session at the right hand; the Hessians seemed more cautious than the rest in their Judgment on the Book of Concord, A. 1576. See these things at length in Hospinian, Ursinus Wendelinus, Massonius Anat. Germ. Part II, and so on.
pass_b_english: So it is plain how tangled others have made the state of this quarrel, and how Lutherans have not always posed it one way.
The Swabians — Brenz, Schmidlin, and the rest who led first — wanted the divine properties poured into the human nature by the union's force, already in the womb.
The Saxons wanted communion of the divine properties of omnipotence, omnipresence, and the like in the assumed flesh, by the exaltation and the session at the right hand.
The Hessians looked more careful than the others in their Judgment on the Book of Concord (1576). Hospinian, Ursinus Wendelinus, Massonius (Anat. Germ. Part II), and others treat this at length.
source_text: UNDE patet, quam involutus fuerit ab aliis Status Controversiae, nec uno semper propositus modo a Lutheranis. Suevi enim, Brentius, Schmidlinus, &c. primi autores, effusionem voluerunt Proprietatum Divinar. in Humanam, vi Unionis, jam in Utero: Saxones Communionem Proprietatum Divinarum Omnipot. Omnipraes. &c. in assumpta Carne, vi Exaltationis & Sessionis a Dextris: Hassi, cautiores reliquis visi in Judicio suo de Libro Concordiae, A. 1576. Quae vide sis fuse apud Hospinianum, Ursinum Wendelinum, Massonium Anat. Germ. P. II. &c.
